title: Minimum width for universal approximation in the uniform norm
open_core: Determine the least width w(d_x, d_y) at which ReLU networks of arbitrary depth are dense in C(K, R^(d_y)) for compact K in R^(d_x).
known_from_memory_to_verify: Park-Yun-Lee-Shin: the L^p answer is max(d_x + 1, d_y); for the uniform norm only bounds are known (Cai; Kim-Min-Park), with a gap when d_y is at least 2.

title: Unconditional lower bounds for multi-layer transformers
open_core: Exhibit an explicit function on n tokens that no transformer with a constant number of layers, polynomial width and logarithmic precision computes, without a complexity-theoretic assumption.
known_from_memory_to_verify: Log-precision transformers lie in uniform TC0 (Merrill-Sabharwal); one-layer communication lower bounds (Peng-Narayanan-Papadimitriou; Sanford-Hsu-Telgarsky); first multi-layer decoder bounds (Chen-Peng-Wu).

title: Length generalisation of transformers (the RASP-L conjecture)
open_core: Transformers trained by gradient descent on bounded-length inputs generalise to longer inputs exactly on the tasks expressible by short programs in a limit-transformer class; prove either direction for trained networks.
known_from_memory_to_verify: Zhou et al.: the conjecture and experiments; Huang et al.: an identification-in-the-limit theorem for an idealised learner.

title: Privacy of the last iterate of noisy stochastic gradient descent for non-convex losses
open_core: Does the Renyi differential privacy of the last iterate of DP-SGD with hidden intermediate states stay bounded in the number of steps for smooth non-convex losses on a bounded domain?
known_from_memory_to_verify: Bounded for convex and strongly convex losses (Chourasia-Ye-Shokri; Altschuler-Talwar); partial non-convex results under dissipativity or clipping.

title: Computation in superposition
open_core: For a network with n neurons, find the largest number m(n) of sparse features on which pairwise logical operations can be computed in superposition with bounded error, with matching upper and lower bounds.
known_from_memory_to_verify: Constructions with m of order n^2 up to logarithmic factors (Hanni et al.; Vaintrob et al.); lower bounds of Adler-Shavit leave polylogarithmic gaps and cover restricted circuits.
